findings: Exact nonce-bearing service command, invocation and group are checked independently of resource properties, so wrong resource limits still permit cleanup only of the authenticated owned service.

Cleanup observes terminal service state, all recorded original PID/start identities gone, and recursive cgroup.procs plus kernel populated metadata twice. Empty direct-child results cannot stand in for whole-tree drain.

Main process capture is required for lifecycle success, and terminal ExecMainPID must match it. A captured descendant cannot substitute for the service main. PID reuse is not the original owner; a same-start zombie/escaped process still blocks drain.

Stop precedes kill-all if needed, with fresh invocation/command ownership checks before each operation and persisted intent. Replaced invocation is never stopped or killed; no unowned numeric PID is signalled.
Any forced cleanup, command error, child failure or nonzero service exit prevents lifecycle success even when the group finally drains.

Existing child supervisor returns successful, while existing pair supervisor returns direct_children_successful. Adapter handles their actual schemas, validates captured/granted/zero-exit/reaped evidence, and requires caller persistence of original binary stdout/stderr before combined terminal receipt.
Malformed supervisor result or output-persistence failure still triggers owned-group cleanup and retains failure. The core never authorizes serial-lock release.
36tests include generated nested cgroups/fake service transitions and actual lightweight Python child/pair executions with existing frozen supervisors; no actual model service operation occurred.
limits: No real systemd model service was started/stopped/killed. Actual service/cgroup integration remains a future serial admission, not established by generated metadata tests.

systemctl has no atomic invocation-ID conditional stop. A cooperating exclusive root lock plus fresh fixed namespace must prevent replacement between authentication and mutation; no adversarial atomicity claim.

The polling budget is at most60seconds; each actual service command separately caps at10seconds. The actual root must enforce its complete wall/resource cleanup budget, retain the serial lock on cleanup failure, and independently verify all scientific receipts.

Full exact source/env/bootstrap/native origin closure, fresh predecessor history, worker successor, service main/rank/helper capture and durable output writer still require complete root integration. Original Nov6 v2 source contract remains non-runnable.
Only known recorded escaped identities are checked outside the group. Arbitrary native-process migration is not sandboxed here; actual service permissions and full launch policy remain required.
